about.title: About
about.heading: Accessibility perspective shaped by lived experience and software practice
about.lead: Siddharth Kalantri is an accessibility-focused software engineer from Bhiwandi, Maharashtra. His work combines screen-reader expertise, self-directed software learning, and practical project building.
about.journeyTitle: A career transition built through adaptation
journey: Siddharth holds a B.Sc. in Drugs and Dyes Chemistry from BNN College, Bhiwandi. After graduation, he worked in his family flour mill business and pursued Flour Milling Technology at the International School of Milling Technology.

A retinal detachment led to glaucoma, and over five to seven years he gradually lost vision in both eyes. He adapted by mastering assistive technologies and built deep daily experience with NVDA and JAWS screen readers.

Around 2022, after online learning became more accessible, he began a focused transition into software development. He now builds web applications, accessibility tools, AI/RAG projects, database-backed systems, and cloud-ready Node.js applications.

accessibility.title: Accessibility Statement
accessibility.heading: Accessibility is a core requirement for FunctionSid
accessibility.lead: This website targets WCAG 2.2 Level AA and is designed for keyboard navigation, semantic HTML, visible focus states, and NVDA and JAWS screen-reader compatibility.
accessibility.commitmentText: Siddharth Kalantri is a blind developer and long-term screen-reader user. That experience shapes the site's structure, navigation, forms, headings, and content clarity.
practices: Skip link appears as the first focusable element.
Every page uses one main heading and semantic landmarks.
Navigation uses active states with aria-current.
Interactive controls retain visible focus indicators.
Contact form fields use explicit labels and required-state markup.
accessibility.testingText: Automated, browser, keyboard, NVDA, and JAWS checks are part of the project quality process.

lawgpt.title: LawGPT
lawgpt.subtitle: Accessible RAG Legal Assistant for Indian Law
lawgpt.imageAlt: LawGPT interface showing a Constitution query with simple English output, inline citations, and source references.
lawgpt.secondaryImageAlt: LawGPT chat interface showing a Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita query with cited legal source references.
lawgpt.summary: An accessible Retrieval-Augmented Generation assistant that explains Indian legal documents in simple English while preserving source transparency through inline citations.
lawgpt.overview: LawGPT is designed for people who need legal text explained clearly without losing the connection to the original source. It works with the Constitution of India and the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023.
lawgpt.problem: Legal documents are dense, formal, and difficult to search. Readers often need both a plain-language explanation and a reliable path back to the exact legal text.
lawgpt.solution: The project combines direct statute lookup, hybrid retrieval, dataset filtering, and cited LLM responses. The interface is keyboard-first and screen-reader friendly.
architecture: Express and EJS render the interface.
A retrieval layer combines regex lookup with hybrid search.
Context blocks are passed to the language model with citation labels.
The answer links back to source text blocks.
accessibility: Keyboard shortcuts for query input, sending, chat log, and source references.
Screen-reader optimized headings, source lists, and plain text fallback.
Inline citations help users verify answers without visual scanning.
challenges: Maintaining legal source accuracy while simplifying language.
Separating Constitution and BNS datasets reliably.
Keeping citations aligned with retrieved context blocks.
lawgpt.outcome: The case study demonstrates accessible AI design, retrieval architecture, and practical source transparency for complex legal content.
future: Add more validation around citation consistency.
Expand multilingual legal explanations after review.

agriquery.title: AgriQuery
agriquery.subtitle: Accessible Agricultural Commodity Price Chatbot
agriquery.imageAlt: AgriQuery homepage showing an accessibility-first chatbot for agricultural commodity prices.
agriquery.secondaryImageAlt: AgriQuery help page explaining how users can ask natural language questions about commodity prices.
agriquery.summary: A web chatbot that helps users ask natural-language questions about official agricultural commodity prices from government data sources.
agriquery.overview: AgriQuery makes daily mandi price information easier to access for farmers, traders, students, and screen-reader users.
agriquery.problem: Government market price data can be difficult to find and interpret. Users may not know the official commodity names or how to search large datasets.
agriquery.solution: The application accepts natural-language queries, handles common commodity names and synonyms, fetches official data, and returns relevant price information in a simple interface.
architecture: Scheduled data import keeps local records current.
Natural-language matching maps user input to commodity data.
Database queries return market records quickly.
accessibility: Semantic HTML and labeled form controls.
Clear status and error messaging for screen readers.
challenges: Balancing fuzzy matching with reliable results.
agriquery.outcome: AgriQuery shows how public data can become a practical, accessible conversational tool.

dectalk-nvda-bridge.title: DECtalk NVDA Bridge
dectalk-nvda-bridge.subtitle: Compatibility Layer for Modern 64-bit NVDA
dectalk-nvda-bridge.status: Completed and maintained for future NVDA releases
dectalk-nvda-bridge.imageAlt: DECtalk NVDA Bridge infographic showing a compatibility bridge between modern 64-bit NVDA and the legacy 32-bit DECtalk engine.
dectalk-nvda-bridge.summary: A compatibility project that restores the classic DECtalk speech synthesizer for modern 64-bit versions of NVDA.
dectalk-nvda-bridge.overview: DECtalk NVDA Bridge preserves access to a legacy speech synthesizer used by many blind computer users while adapting it for newer NVDA architecture.
dectalk-nvda-bridge.problem: Modern NVDA releases require 64-bit compatibility, while the original DECtalk speech engine is a 32-bit Windows component.
dectalk-nvda-bridge.solution: The bridge keeps the original DECtalk engine untouched and uses NVDA SynthDriverHost32 to connect modern NVDA with the legacy speech component.
architecture: NVDA 2026.1 runs as the modern 64-bit screen reader.
The original 32-bit DECtalk engine produces speech output.
accessibility: Preserves a familiar speech option for blind NVDA users.
Supports clean startup, shutdown, and stable speech output.
Maintains compatibility without changing the original synthesizer.
challenges: Testing across modern NVDA behavior while preserving legacy output.
dectalk-nvda-bridge.outcome: The project restores DECtalk support on NVDA 2026.1 and demonstrates practical compatibility engineering for assistive technology.
future: Continue compatibility testing for future NVDA releases.
Improve documentation for installation and troubleshooting.

a11y-insights.title: A11Y Insights
a11y-insights.subtitle: Educational Platform for Web Accessibility
a11y-insights.imageAlt: Homepage of the A11Y Insights website showing the main navigation and accessibility learning platform.
a11y-insights.secondaryImageAlt: A11Y Insights accessibility tools page showing WCAG testing tools and evaluation resources.
a11y-insights.summary: An educational web platform that helps developers and students understand accessibility concepts, WCAG principles, and testing tools.
a11y-insights.overview: A11Y Insights organizes accessibility education into a structured learning experience with practical testing resources.
a11y-insights.problem: Accessibility learning resources are often scattered, making it harder for beginners to understand WCAG concepts and choose useful testing tools.
a11y-insights.solution: The site combines accessibility principles, auditing guidance, browser extensions, case studies, and learning resources in one accessible platform.
architecture: Static educational sections organize WCAG and testing content.
JavaScript supports search and interactive learning areas.
Responsive layouts keep content readable across devices.
accessibility: Accessibility is the project subject and implementation standard.
Content covers perceivable, operable, understandable, and robust design.
Screens and resources explain real testing tools.
challenges: Organizing a large amount of educational material.
Keeping beginner explanations useful without oversimplifying professional accessibility work.
a11y-insights.outcome: The project demonstrates front-end development, information architecture, accessibility education, and WCAG-centered content design.
future: Improve search and learner progress tracking.

stream-ripper.title: Stream-Ripper
stream-ripper.subtitle: NVDA Add-on for Accessible Audio Stream Workflows
stream-ripper.imageAlt: NVDA Input Gestures dialog showing keyboard shortcuts available for the Stream-Ripper add-on.
stream-ripper.summary: An accessibility-first NVDA add-on that detects supported media URLs, extracts audio streams with yt-dlp, and supports FFmpeg conversion.
stream-ripper.overview: Stream-Ripper gives screen-reader users a keyboard-driven workflow for extracting and converting supported online audio streams.
stream-ripper.problem: Audio extraction workflows often require command-line tools and manual steps that are not designed around screen-reader productivity.
stream-ripper.solution: The add-on monitors supported URLs, manages extraction and conversion tasks, and announces progress through NVDA.
architecture: NVDA add-on code runs inside the screen reader environment.
Clipboard monitoring detects supported media links.
FFmpeg handles optional conversion and output formats.
accessibility: Screen-reader announcements for status and progress.
Accessible settings dialog and native NVDA integration.
challenges: Integrating external tools without making users work in the command line.
Keeping progress feedback clear for screen-reader users.
stream-ripper.outcome: The project demonstrates how accessibility and automation can reduce friction in everyday media workflows.
future: Document supported URL patterns more fully.
